bug_semantics: CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion in liquidjs `{% layout %}` / `{% block %}`. In STORE mode, `src/tags/block.ts` `getBlockRender` records a per-name render function in `ctx.getRegister('blocks')[this.block]`. When a child template nests a block inside another block of the same name (including anonymous `{%block%}`), the inner tag looks up that register, wraps the outer render as `renderChild`, and overwrites the slot. OUTPUT-mode layout then calls the inner wrapper; the outer templates still contain the inner same-name block, which looks up the same register and re-enters `renderChild` with no cycle check. Recursion allocates renderer/emitter frames until the Node.js heap OOMs (~4GB). The 2016 layout/block implementation stored rendered HTML strings and could not form this call cycle. GHSA-4rc3-7j7w-m548 / CVE-2026-41311 (NVD Analyzed, not withdrawn) patch the path in `e2311dfd6e82f73509308aa8a3a1fafc92e226f0` by pushing the current Tag onto a `blockStack` register and throwing `block tag cannot be nested`. Advisory range is `< 10.25.7` (first_patched 10.25.7); the fix commit is already an ancestor of tag v10.25.6.
flaw_origin: The recursive wrap was first written in `a3af44dc10fda3fab2285f9423e3d8a2919c04a5` (`feat: support {{block.super}}, see #38`, 2021-01-24) by maintainer harttle. That commit replaced HTML-valued `blocks[name]` with render-function wrapping (`extendedBlockRender(new BlockDrop(() => defaultBlockRender(superBlock)))`) so `{{block.super}}` could re-enter the parent body. The lookup is by block name only and never tracks in-flight tags, so a same-name nested block aliases the outer function and becomes a self-call. Immediate parent `0e0dc2adf0dd4f06ee03e6fb5c5f377e3434a5fc` still stores HTML (`childDefined` / `blocks[this.block] = html`) and has no `getBlockRender`, `BlockDrop`, or wrap. Later commits (aea34418 streamed emitter, 92992689/1380ac93 Tag-class move `src/builtin/tags/block.ts` → `src/tags/block.ts`, 025c40f0 BlockDrop signature) only refactor the same wrap; they are not BICs.
